fields.summary: Ad-hoc task max fail delay not working as intended

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
There are a few problems with the current implementation of max fail delays:
 # There was a maths error in the original issue requirements implementing the maximum attempts value (MAX_RETRY), so instead of the intended outcome of stopping retries after 24+ hours, it stops after just 4 hours. This causes some unnecessary complexity (or breaks the implementation) when trying to implement the new max fail notification (MDL-79131), because the max retry time doesn't match the 24 hour notification requirement.
 # There are references to the null option being "unlimited retries", which was designed as a temporary measure while "no retry" was being implemented prior to a proper max fail delay being implemented, so should not still be usable.
 # The combination of MAX_RETRY when setting a task's initial attempts available means we are bypassing the task object's own _attemptsavailable_ property, which adds unnecessary complexity and limitations on that functionality (it locks tasks into two possible starting values, preventing tasks from properly using {_}set_attempts_available(){_}).

These issues can all be solved as follows:
 # In adhoc_task.php, change the default value for the [attemptsavailable|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/main/lib/classes/task/adhoc_task.php#L49-L50] property from _null_ to *12* (which is the number of attempts required to hit the maximum 24 hour backoff), and  in the docblock remove "or null for unlimited" as well as null as a data type (it should just be {_}int{_}).
 # In the same file, update both the [set_attempts_available|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/main/lib/classes/task/adhoc_task.php#L183C21-L183C43] and [get_attempts_available|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/main/lib/classes/task/adhoc_task.php#L192] so the imports/exports only allow _int_ (not nullable), and update their docblocks to remove references to null being a valid value/meaning unlimited.
 # In manager.php, change this:
{code:java}$record->attemptsavailable = $task->retry_until_success() ? self::MAX_RETRY : 1; {code}
To this: 
{code:java}$record->attemptsavailable = $task->retry_until_success() ? $record->attemptsavailable : 1;
{code}
 # Completely remove all references to the _MAX_RETRY_ constant (including removing the constant itself), because it is no longer needed.

The result of the above is that the correct number of retries are attempted, they are properly fetched from the task object (which removes the need for the constant), we now support (and require) a valid, finite number of retries to be defined, and we still ensure that if a task has defined that it's a "no retry" task, that will still override  the number of attempts to 1.

 
h4. Steps to reproduce:

*Prerequisites.* 
Install the testing plugin [^moodle-tool_test_tasks.zip]
It can be found attached to this issue, and it can be installed with the zip package from "site admin" / "Plugins" / "Install plugins"

*Adhoc task - Available attempts*
 # Locate the file [^test_MDL-81000.php]in your root folder
 # Execute it with the following command from root: 
{code:java}php test_MDL-82000.php {code}

 # Check these values are in the results 
{code:java}Initial values: 
- Attempts available = 12 - Fail delay = 0
Run task:

- Attempts available = 10 - Fail delay = 120

- Attempts available = 3 - Fail delay = 15360
- Attempts available = 2 - Fail delay = 30720
- Attempts available = 1 - Fail delay = 61440
- Attempts available = 0 - Fail delay = 86400 {code}

fields.summary: Private files area quota applies when unzipping to non-private file areas.

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
Plugins such as mod_scorm use zips, which are unzipped and stored in the mdl_files when saved.

Since MDL-74641, there is a check added here that the unzipped file size does not exceed the "Private files space" config:

[https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/e567c21d6edb902e652fcbf1aaf4a49a82579f84/lib/filestorage/zip_packer.php#L457-L462]

Two issues with this:
 # This is confusing for end users, since mod_scorm doesn't touch the private files area, but this setting "Private files space" affects it. I believe this should be at a minimum renamed to "unzip file area quota"
 # It checks the existing usage of files in the users private file area, regardless if the file being unzipped is in the private file area (in scorm, they are not)

A better solution would be being able to define max file sizes per-area (so for example, scorm could be 200mb but private files could be 1mb, etc...), and then check the respective area for existing usage.

|{color:#000000}mv config.php config.real.php{color}|

Restart php-fpm, or apache, to ensure the realpath cache is cleared.

Browse to: {{admin/tool/mfa/factor/email/email.php?instance=1}}

This provides a small buffer in case the major release is delayed. If any of other details in the security.txt need to be amended, they should also be completed at the same time. We should also check the RFC in case of any changes (see the [Github repo|https://github.com/securitytxt/security-txt] to check if any versions have been released since the previous LMS release).

usable only once - the token must not allow more than one registration

We just need to validate it as an optional field, and ensure that it's conditionally added to the requests headers as a bearer token.

fields.summary: Bad param type validation on login_hint strips login_hint after cookie check redirect

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: LTI provider
components.description: Moodle components enrol_lti and auth_lti

fields.description:
I've noticed this bug during testing using the LTI certification suite.

This is a bug surfaced by MDL-80835, which will need to be fixed on security branches (as 80835 was landed there too to fix upcoming browser changes).

Basically, this is what's happened:
 # We always used a required_param() to validate the presence of login_hint param. ONLY the presence of it. The further validation of that param was left to library code, where the real value was taken from $_REQUEST.
 -- This all worked fine, despite the param type (PARAM_INT) being wrong and actually silently converting strings to the number 0. It should be PARAM_RAW, since this is a platform-controlled value and can be a GUID/whatever. We didn't see this since we weren't USING that value, only checking it's existence in the request.
 # Now, since MDL-80835, we are USING that value, as we pass it into a cookie check and redirect back, only then continuing with the OIDC login. Basically, this means $_REQUEST will now contain the bad value (0 in some cases, depending on what's being cast to int) instead of the original (likely string) value, since we've redirected to self as part of the cookie check.
 # This then results in possible launch validation failure, since the value passed to LtiOidcLogin::validateOidcLogin() can be 0, and the check used there (it's library code) is an if (empty()) , which of course fails. See [the relevant code here|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/63569a4776327f18a4edcf2e27effcedbd758420/lib/lti1p3/src/LtiOidcLogin.php#L53]. If something is cast to 0 and ends up here, we'll throw an exception and block an otherwise valid launch.

Basically, the crux of the issue is that a login_hint like "93F589A7-C501-41BA-A471-C3AE8C804CE5" will be cleaned, through PARAM_INT, to the integer 93, which isn't right. Sometimes, depending on the string, this can end up converting to the integer 0, which causes launch failures.
